Raster rankings were scale-dependent: Google Open Buildings Temporal (OBT) performed best at 10\,m (F1 = 0.680), whereas WSF Tracker led at 100\,m (F1 = 0.904) but substantially overestimated reference building area (relative bias = 1.845). Raster accuracy increased with building density ($ρ=0.58$--$0.75$), while smaller candidate footprints were disproportionately associated with vector false positives. Temporal alignment improved WSF Tracker mean city-level F1 by 0.060. These findings demonstrate that product reliability depends on representation, spatial scale, and settlement context, providing a reproducible framework for assessing the suitability of EO-derived urban information for different applications.

Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.title: A$^3$PreCore: Robust Rigid Registration for Native FLAIR-Space Brain-Mask Transfer
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.summary: Reliable brain-mask transfer into native fluid-attenuated inversion recovery (FLAIR) space can fail when T1-to-FLAIR rigid registration is unstable. We developed A$^3$PreCore, a six-degree-of-freedom rigid-registration strategy that aligns the full bias-corrected T1-weighted image to native FLAIR using normalized mutual information while preserving the established T1-space anatomical mask. We also introduced extended quantitative quality control (E-QC), which characterizes mask extent, field-of-view-relative position, FLAIR intensity support, boundary support, inferior morphology, and pairwise geometric disagreement. In 78 participants with paired T1-weighted and FLAIR imaging, A$^3$PreCore was compared with fsl_anat and the Brain Extraction Tool (BET). Gross rigid-body misregistration occurred in 21/78 fsl_anat outputs (26.9%) and 0/78 A$^3$PreCore outputs (exact two-sided McNemar p=9.54 x 10^-7). Among 57 participants without gross fsl_anat misregistration, A$^3$PreCore preserved close agreement (median Dice=0.993; median paired Delta NMI=-0.00007, p=0.429). A$^3$PreCore remained broadly concordant with BET (median Dice=0.955), with less inferior and extracranial extension in representative comparisons. Method-blinded neuroscientists ranked A$^3$PreCore first in 35/40 participants (87.5%). E-QC additionally exposed severe orientation-related disagreement not evident from global descriptors or centroid displacement alone. These findings support A$^3$PreCore as a robust native-FLAIR brain-mask transfer strategy and E-QC as a complementary framework for multidimensional mask characterization and participant-specific geometric quality control.

Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.title: Medical Imaging Classification with Cold-Atom Reservoir Computing using Auto-Encoders and Surrogate-Driven Training
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.summary: We introduce a hybrid quantum-classical pipeline, based on neutral-atom reservoir computing, for medical image classification, focusing on the binary classification task of polyp detection. To deal effectively with the high dimensionality, we integrate a guided auto-encoder. This pipeline learns compact and discriminative representations of image data that are also well-suited for quantum reservoir computing. A key challenge in such systems is the non-differentiable nature of quantum measurements, which creates a 'gradient barrier' for standard training. We overcome this barrier by incorporating a differentiable surrogate model that emulates the quantum layer, enabling end-to-end backpropagation through the entire system. This guided training process is jointly optimized for classification accuracy and for faithful image recovery from the auto-encoder. The learned latent representations are encoded as pulse detuning parameters within a Rydberg Hamiltonian, and quantum embeddings are subsequently obtained through expectation values. These embeddings are then passed to a linear classifier. Our simulations show that this method outperforms some traditional approaches that use PCA or unguided autoencoders. We also conduct ablation studies to assess the impact of various quantum and training parameters, demonstrating the robustness and flexibility of our proposed pipeline for real-world medical imaging applications, even in the current NISQ era.
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.comment: 8 pages, 6 figures. Accepted to the 2025 IEEE International Conference on Quantum AI (IEEE QAI). Supported by FCT and the Open Quantum Institute (OQI). v2: corrects the stated Rabi frequency to $Ω= 2π$ rad/$μ$s

Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.title: LightHybridNet: A Lightweight Hybrid Deep Learning Framework for Efficient Multi-Label Ophthalmic Disease Classification in Imbalanced Fundus Images
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.summary: Eye diseases are a major global cause of blindness and vision impairment, highlighting the need for accurate and early diagnosis to prevent further deterioration. Despite advances in medical imaging, classifying retinal diseases from fundus images remains challenging due to the complexity and subtlety of visual features. This study aims to develop and validate LightHybridNet, a novel lightweight hybrid deep learning framework, to improve the classification of eye diseases from fundus images. The model incorporates architectural features, such as depthwise separable convolutions and compound scaling mechanisms, to enhance diagnostic accuracy and robustness. To validate the model, the ODIR-5K dataset, comprising 8 disease categories, was used. To enhance image quality, pre-processing approaches were applied, including histogram equalisation, colour space conversion, and contrast adjustment, resulting in high-resolution images. Furthermore, image augmentation was employed to increase the dataset size, thereby improving the model's ability to generalise during training. The hybrid architecture helps the model concentrate on relevant image regions while capturing and integrating details at different scales, significantly improving classification performance. To evaluate its effectiveness, the model was compared with transfer-learning models. The results show that LightHybridNet outperforms the baselines, achieving a weighted F1-score of 91.51%, a macro AUC of 98.26%, and a Cohen's Kappa of 90.14% on the validation set. Furthermore, model interpretability was enhanced using explainable AI methods, including Grad-CAM, to identify and emphasise features influencing the decision-making process. LightHybridNet represents a promising advancement in automated ocular disease detection, offering improved diagnostic reliability for clinical use.
authors: Hem Raj Dadral Najam Ul Hasan

Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.title: Synergistic Vision-Language Reinforcement Enables Scalable On-Demand Analysis across Diverse Clinical Tasks
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.summary: Accurate segmentation of tumors and organs-at-risk is essential for oncology but remains time-consuming and expertise-intensive. Existing AI systems often require manual spatial prompts or task-specific retraining, while generic class labels provide limited guidance for heterogeneous disease targets. Here we present SyRe, a text-prompted segmentation foundation model based on Synergistic vision-language Reinforcement, which strengthens bidirectional interaction between visual and linguistic representations. We introduce Color Region Description (CRD) to generate region-level semantic supervision and construct SyReData, comprising 20 million image-mask-description triplets across 9 modalities and 229 segmentation tasks. Training with diversified prompt formats enables single-target, multi-target and open-ended segmentation, together with invalid-prompt rejection. SyRe achieves accurate segmentation across diverse clinical scenarios, with strong gains on disease-related targets. Evaluation on 28 unseen external datasets, including 17 cancer types, 3 non-cancer diseases and multinational in-house cohorts, demonstrates generalization under distribution shift. Beyond spatial overlap, SyRe-generated masks preserve quantitative pathology information. Across five retrospective tumor imaging cohorts spanning CT and MRI, radiomics derived from these masks stratify survival and improve prognostic modeling over clinical baselines. Clinician-in-the-loop refinement further supports case-level correction. These results establish SyRe as a generalizable framework for scalable quantitative oncology analysis and clinician-guided segmentation.

Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.title: SCI-Mamba: Unsupervised Learning based Low-Light Image Enhancement for Non-Cooperative Spacecraft
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.summary:
Low-light visual perception acts as the core visual foundation for on-orbit servicing missions targeting non-cooperative spacecraft, supporting autonomous rendezvous, pose estimation, component detection and robotic capture operations. Spaceborne imagery suffers from severe low-light degradation, while the extreme scarcity of paired normal/low-light space samples severely limits the generalization capacity of supervised enhancement algorithms. To address this practical bottleneck, this paper proposes SCI-Mamba, an unsupervised enhancement network for low-light orbital spacecraft observations. The proposed framework unites self-calibrated unsupervised learning, linear-complexity VMamba architecture and Retinex physical priors, delivering a lightweight enhancement pipeline adaptable to resource-limited spaceborne hardware. We construct Space Dark-1.0, a dedicated low-light spacecraft dataset integrating real orbital footage, darkroom hardware-in-the-loop measurements and physically constrained synthetic data covering diverse illumination, motion and attitude conditions. Comprehensive comparisons with CNN-, Transformer- and prevailing Mamba-based approaches verify the advantages of SCI-Mamba in visual authenticity, color fidelity and inference speed. The proposed framework provides a practical low-light enhancement solution for close-proximity non-cooperative space operations.
  The code is available at https://github.com/bitswh/SCI-Mamba

Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.title: Perceptual Characterization of Scan-induced Artifacts in Dynamic 3D Meshes
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.summary: Dynamic meshes reconstructed from real-world scenes often exhibit scan-induced artifacts such as surface jitter and missing geometry, which strongly impact perceived visual quality. Objective assessment remains challenging due to the absence of artifact-free ground truth and limited perceptual understanding of artifact interactions. This paper presents a systematic and controlled perceptual study of scan-induced artifacts in dynamic meshes, focusing on surface jitter and holes. To enable systematic analysis, we introduce a physically grounded artifact synthesis framework in which holes are synthesized using a reconstruction uncertainty model derived from multi-view geometry. The study reveals asymmetric cross-artifact interactions, non-additive integration, and motion-dependent temporal masking. Based on these findings, we propose a compact, perceptually grounded no-reference quality assessment framework that encodes the observed perceptual mechanisms.

Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.title: AdaFrame: Hierarchical Multimodal Deduplication with Adaptive Information Budgeting for Cost-Efficient Video Advertisement Analysis
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.summary: Uniform frame sampling for vision-language model (VLM)-based video analysis often floods multimodal backbones with redundant content, while existing keyframe selection methods are typically optimized for human viewing rather than downstream extraction accuracy. We propose AdaFrame, a content-adaptive preprocessing cascade that reduces visual redundancy without sacrificing extraction fidelity. Three progressively finer filters, perceptual hashing, learned perceptual image patch similarity (LPIPS), and CLIP-based semantic clustering, efficiently eliminate redundant frames before costly cross-modal inference. Per-video frame budgets are determined using Intrinsic Semantic Dimensionality (ISD), which estimates each video's semantic complexity through singular value decomposition of its frame embeddings. Experiments on 500 video advertisements from the Pitt Ads Dataset show that AdaFrame reduces the frame count by 48 percent and VLM inference cost by 75 percent compared with uniform sampling, while achieving 86.0 percent topic accuracy, an improvement of 1.6 percentage points, and 79.4 percent sentiment accuracy, an improvement of 7.5 percentage points.

Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.title: OmniCompass: A Holistic Benchmark for Omni-Modal Video Grounding and Understanding
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.summary: With the rapid development of multimodal large language models (MLLMs), evaluating their video understanding capabilities has become increasingly important. Existing video understanding benchmarks cover only part of the evaluation dimensions, limiting systematic diagnosis of omni-modal video understanding. We introduce OmniCompass, a holistic benchmark for omni-modal video grounding and understanding. OmniCompass defines two evaluation tracks: OmniCompass-VL assesses vision-language models on tasks requiring visual evidence, while OmniCompass-AV assesses omni-modal models on tasks requiring joint audio-visual evidence. Each track includes three complementary tasks: temporal grounding (TG), spatial grounding (SG), and question answering (QA), assessing when a referenced target appears, where it is, and what happens. QA covers five perception and three reasoning categories in OmniCompass-VL, and three perception and two reasoning categories in OmniCompass-AV. OmniCompass-VL contains 820 videos and 2,460 instances across domains and three duration types: short, medium, and long. A narrative- and audio-rich subset forms OmniCompass-AV with 240 videos and 720 instances. Each instance is evaluated under two paired settings: text-only and text+image, specifying the same target through text and visual-language guidance. All instances are manually annotated with multi-round quality verification. Evaluations of 50 MLLMs show that open-source models still lag behind proprietary counterparts, particularly in audio-visual understanding. Precise temporal and spatial grounding remains challenging even for leading models, and their predictions still exhibit inconsistencies across the paired target specifications.
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.comment: Homepage: https://omnicompass.netlify.app/

Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.title: GeoReader: Learning Latent Geometry for Spatial Reasoning in Vision-Language Models
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.summary: Vision-language models (VLMs) struggle with metric and multi-view relationships that remain implicit in RGB observations. Geometry foundation models recover this structure from RGB, but existing methods either fuse the estimated features with visual tokens and learn to use them from question answering alone, or align VLM latents with geometry features. Capturing geometry, however, does not ensure its use: zeroing the aligned latents of a released feature-alignment model leaves its accuracy unchanged. We introduce GeoReader, a framework that learns geometric representations for the VLM that reads them. First, we train lightweight Geometric Readers to produce continuous input tokens, supervising them with geometry descriptions decoded by a frozen VLM, so that the Readers express geometry in a form the target model can already read. We then freeze the Readers to preserve this interface while fine-tuning the VLM on spatial QA, with geometry injection conditioned on the question. Geometry descriptions serve only as training targets: at inference, the VLM answers directly from the continuous geometric tokens without generating a geometry chain of thought. With geometry predicted from RGB images, our approach reaches 94.3 on MindCube-Tiny with Qwen3-VL-4B and, with a multi-source QA mixture, an average of 72.5 across six additional spatial benchmarks with Qwen3.5-9B. These results suggest that a useful geometric representation is one the receiving model can use, not merely one from which geometry can be reconstructed.
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.comment: 35 pages, 11 figures, 15 tables; Project Page at https://iris0329.github.io/georeader-homepage/ GitHub Repo at https://github.com/iris0329/GeoReader

Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.title: Decomposing and Predicting Annotation Disagreement in Harmful Content Across Languages
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.summary: Annotator disagreement is increasingly recognized as a meaningful property of subjective tasks, rather than merely noise to be removed. Predicting which items are likely to be contested could help allocate annotation effort and route difficult cases to human review. We propose predicting disagreement from interpretable semantic properties of the text. An LLM answers a set of binary questions covering harmful-content characteristics, disagreement-related cues such as borderline severity and missing context, and language-sensitive cues such as local slurs. A classifier predicts disagreement from these answers, and we analyze which questions contribute most to the predictions. Across four datasets in English, German, and Turkish and three open-weight LLMs, our structured question features outperform direct prompting by 10.5 ROC-AUC points and the strongest text-based baselines by 5.0 points. A compact subset of eight questions performs within 1.5 ROC-AUC points of the full twenty-question set. In leave-one-dataset-out evaluation, models retain roughly 90-95% of their in-domain ROC-AUC. Across models and datasets, questions about derogation, missing context, and decision boundaries serve as the strongest predictors, suggesting that what makes harmful content contested is partly observable in the text.

Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.title: DualAffect: Dual-Path Paralinguistic Integration for Generative Audiovisual Emotion Understanding
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.summary: Understanding human emotion is essential for multimodal systems that interpret both the content of an interaction and the speaker's expressive state. However, connecting paralinguistic cues to generated answers remains challenging, particularly when vocal expression diverges from visual appearance. We propose DualAffect, a dual-path architecture that integrates visually conditioned acoustic features and temporally organized acoustic tokens into a shared language decoder. The two pathways reuse the same acoustic encoding. The fusion pathway associates sound with visual content through visual queries, while the direct pathway compresses the valid acoustic sequence into ordered tokens through an independent projector. This design gives the decoder access to both joint audiovisual context and acoustic evidence organized along its own timeline. Mixed-task adaptation with task-dependent output preservation supports emotion recognition and general audiovisual question answering within the same model. DualAffect achieves an average metric of 67.89 on CA-MER and accuracies of 62.88% on the EmotionTalk test set and 49.87% on Daily-Omni. Pathway interventions show that the trained decoder uses direct acoustic evidence alongside existing fusion. With model parameters and fusion inputs fixed, zeroing the direct tokens reduces EmotionTalk validation accuracy by 9.75 percentage points and the CA-MER average metric by 2.66 points. The largest CA-MER subset effect occurs when the overall emotion agrees with audio but differs from vision. These findings identify acoustic representation organization as a practical design axis for connecting paralinguistic perception to unified audiovisual generation. Code is available at https://github.com/YiboWang2002/DualAffect.
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.comment: 10 pages, 3 figures

Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.title: Beyond Forced Modality Balance: Intrinsic Information Budgets for Multimodal Learning
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.summary: Multimodal models often converge to a dominant-modality solution, in which a stronger, faster-converging modality overshadows weaker ones. This modality imbalance causes suboptimal performance. Existing methods attempt to balance different modalities by reweighting gradients or losses. However, they overlook the fact that each modality has finite information capacity. In this work, we propose IIBalance, a multimodal learning framework that aligns the modality contributions with Intrinsic Information Budgets (IIB). We propose a task-grounded estimator of each modality's IIB, transforming its capacity into a global prior over modality contributions. Anchored by the highest-budget modality, we design a prototype-based relative alignment mechanism that corrects semantic drift only when weaker modalities deviate from their budgeted potential, rather than forcing imitation. During inference, we propose a probabilistic gating module that integrates the global budgets with sample-level uncertainty to generate calibrated fusion weights. Experiments on three representative benchmarks demonstrate that IIBalance consistently outperforms state-of-the-art balancing methods and achieves better utilization of complementary modality cues. Our code is available at: https://github.com/XiongZechang/IIBalance.
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.comment: 6 pages, 4 figures, paper accepted by ICME 2026

Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.title: KMMMU: Evaluation of Massive Multi-discipline Multimodal Understanding in Korean Language and Context
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.summary: Multimodal evaluation is strengthened when benchmarks reflect the languages, institutions, and disciplinary conventions that shape expert visual reasoning. We introduce KMMMU, a native Korean benchmark built from Korean-native examination materials. KMMMU contains 3,466 questions spanning nine disciplines and nine visual modality categories. For targeted evaluation on challenging questions and Korean-specific knowledge, we additionally provide KMMMU-Adv and KMMMU-Local, respectively. Experiments show that the strongest evaluated open-weight model reaches 42.05% on the KMMMU, while the best evaluated proprietary model achieves 52.42% on the KMMMU-Adv. Performance varies substantially across disciplines and answer formats, with Korean-specific questions showing gaps of up to 13.43%. Error analysis suggests that inspected failures often involve convention-to-label mapping, few-shot symbolic induction, localized knowledge recall, and domain-specific standards, not reasoning depth alone. KMMMU provides a testbed for native Korean expert-level multimodal understanding beyond English-centric or translation-based evaluation.
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.comment: 8 pages

Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.title: Deep Learning for Atmospheric Turbulence Mitigation: A Comparison Between GANs and Transformers
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.summary: Atmospheric turbulence creates complex spatial and temporal distortions that significantly reduce image quality. This work compares two deep learning methods for turbulence reduction: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) and Transformer-based models. Both methods are trained and tested on the SOTIS dataset, which includes multi-frame sequences under different turbulence conditions with ground truth references. Our results show an important finding: GAN-based models perform better in severely degraded, low-quality situations, while Transformer-based models achieve better results in moderate to high-quality settings, especially in correcting geometric distortions. We also enhance the Turbulence Mitigation Transformer (TMT) by introducing a refined training strategy, an augmented input design that includes a temporally averaged frame as prior structural information, and a modified loss function that incorporates the Structural Similarity Index (SSIM). These improvements lead to consistent performance gains across various turbulence conditions. Overall, this study provides an in-depth evaluation of deep learning methods for turbulence reduction and offers practical guidance for selecting models in different imaging environments.
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.comment: Published in the Journal of Electronic Imaging

Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.title: High-resolution retinal matrix imaging via computational motion and aberration correction
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.summary: High-resolution optical imaging of the human retina is essential for diagnosing ophthalmic and neurodegenerative diseases. While adaptive optics combined with coherence gating can resolve retinal structures at the cellular scale, it requires complex, costly, and cumbersome hardware to physically correct for ocular aberrations and motion. Matrix imaging offers a powerful digital alternative by leveraging wave linearity to undo aberrations and multiple scattering; however, its in vivo deployment has been hindered by continuous, involuntary eye movements that destroy phase coherence during acquisition. Here, we overcome this fundamental barrier and demonstrate the first in vivo reflection matrix imaging of the human retina using an ultra-simplified optical setup without physical correctors. We introduce a fully computational framework that tracks and compensates for multi-axial ocular motion directly from raw interferometric data, thereby restoring the phase coherence of a multi-spectral distortion matrix. This enables local, high-order aberration correction to achieve diffraction-limited, volumetric imaging of retinal tissues. By shifting the hardware burden to physics-guided numerical computation, this paradigm opens the way for accessible, non-invasive, and high-resolution digital ophthalmology.

Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.title: Per-Bundle, Pre-Reconstruction Inversion for Temporal CT: Flux-Compensation Design and Multi-Patient Generalization
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.summary: Paper 1 established the per-bundle statistical limits of Temporal CT (TCT) and benchmarked a learned prior on a single patient at a uniform incident count $N_0$. This paper lifts both restrictions. SNN2, a Gauss-Newton estimator, converges to the per-bundle Poisson maximum-likelihood solution and is the prior-free baseline. N$_0$FC, a bow-tie and tube-current-modulation co-design, compresses within-bundle photon-flux dynamic range. V8c is a neural-network residual corrector trained on a 19-patient corpus stratified by water-equivalent diameter (WED). T2bp, a per-patient empirical-Bayes post-processor, combines per-bundle Poisson likelihoods with a prior built from the patient's own bundles; it requires no training, so it cannot inherit a mismatched training prior. Results use Paper 1's bias-charged Dose Inflation Factor (DIF), extended to per-ray budgets. V8c beats SNN2 on in-distribution patients under baseline acquisition but fails out of distribution. Composed with SNN2, T2bp matches or beats T2bp$\circ$V8c on three of four N$_0$FC test cells (WED 207-342 mm), with the largest gains on the high-WED and out-of-distribution patients, and trails by 3% on the fourth. On 23 non-test corpus volumes, N$_0$FC with closed-loop tube-current modulation lowers the per-volume median middle-path Cramer-Rao floor, as a DIF, from 23-48 under baseline acquisition to 3.3-6.3, near the equal-attenuation value 13/3; T2bp$\circ$SNN2 reaches this floor without training, its mean squared error 0.74-1.26 times the floor (median 0.89) over the bulk of each volume. Acquisition co-design removes most of the attenuation-contrast penalty, and a training-free estimator attains the resulting limit. The remaining three- to six-fold gap to dose parity with single-source CT, and the high-attenuation tail, are the target of inter-bundle priors in later work.
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.comment: 52 pages (29 main text, 23 supplementary material), 7 figures, 14 tables. Paper 2 of a series; companion to arXiv:2604.10934. Preliminary version: the 48-cell corpus results will be recomputed with the truth-free T2bp configuration (see "Note on this version")

Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.title: Perceptual Characterization of Scan-induced Artifacts in Dynamic 3D Meshes
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.summary: Dynamic meshes reconstructed from real-world scenes often exhibit scan-induced artifacts such as surface jitter and missing geometry, which strongly impact perceived visual quality. Objective assessment remains challenging due to the absence of artifact-free ground truth and limited perceptual understanding of artifact interactions. This paper presents a systematic and controlled perceptual study of scan-induced artifacts in dynamic meshes, focusing on surface jitter and holes. To enable systematic analysis, we introduce a physically grounded artifact synthesis framework in which holes are synthesized using a reconstruction uncertainty model derived from multi-view geometry. The study reveals asymmetric cross-artifact interactions, non-additive integration, and motion-dependent temporal masking. Based on these findings, we propose a compact, perceptually grounded no-reference quality assessment framework that encodes the observed perceptual mechanisms.

Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.title: DoReMe: Dual optimization of Reconstruction and Motion estimation for self-navigated free-breathing abdominal MRI using Gaussian Splatting
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.summary: Purpose: Free-breathing abdominal MRI is limited by respiratory motion, which introduces image artifacts and k-space inconsistencies. Existing reconstruction approaches often depend on pre-estimated motion fields or external respiratory surrogate signals. We propose a coupled reconstruction-motion estimation algorithm for self-navigated free-breathing acquisition, in which motion is represented by compact Gaussian primitives and jointly refined with the image estimates during iterative reconstruction. Methods: An iterative reconstruction that alternates between data consistency updates and motion modelling was proposed. Respiratory motion was represented using Gaussian primitives. A Gaussian splatting was integrated into the reconstruction algorithm. The method was evaluated on self-navigated free-breathing Cartesian gradient-echo (GRE) acquisition in four healthy volunteers, including retrospective scan shortening experiments, and was compared with regularized compressed sensing (CS) reconstruction. Results: Respiratory motion states were reconstructed in approximately 1.5 min. Compared with CS, the proposed method improved visual image quality, particularly in coronal liver views, and better preserved anatomical structures in retrospectively shortened acquisitions. These findings provide proof of concept for the proposed method. Conclusion: The proposed coupled reconstruction-motion estimation algorithm improved visual image quality compared with CS alone. Gaussian primitives provided a compact and sufficiently flexible representation of nonrigid respiratory motion with practical runtime, supporting further scanner integration and validation in larger cohorts.

Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.title: Focus, Align, and Diffuse: Time-Series-Aware Keyframe Diffusion for Cardiac Dynamic Synthesis from Sparse Observations
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.summary: Dense cardiac dynamics are essential for assessing cardiac function, yet in practice clinicians often observe only extremely sparse measurements. However, recovering full dynamics from such sparsity is a highly ill-posed problem due to the lack of temporal cues. While auxiliary time-series signals like ECG provide physiological guidance, effectively exploiting them is challenging due to the cross-modal representation gap and phase misalignment. In this work, we present CardioFAD, a Focus--Align--Diffuse paradigm that reformulates sparse cardiac dynamic synthesis as a recoverability--alignability anchor discovery problem. Our core insight is that resolving extreme temporal ambiguity requires a compact set of anchor states that are both sufficient to recover the visual trajectory and reliable for ECG--visual alignment. We therefore learn motion-salient keyframes under two complementary principles: trajectory sufficiency, which preserves trajectory-critical intra-modal motion content, and anchor alignment, which promotes consistent inter-modal correspondence at these anchors. We implement the Focus and Align modules optimized by the two aspects. Diffuse then performs two-stage generation by first synthesizing keyframes and subsequently interpolating the remaining frames. Extensive experiments on cardiac MRI and echocardiography videos demonstrate superior visual quality, temporal coherence, and improved functional consistency under the extreme one-shot regime.

Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.title: Simplifying and Improving On-Policy Distillation for Few-Step Diffusion
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.summary: Few-step distillation reduces the sampling cost of diffusion and flow models, but existing approaches often require auxiliary score models or specialized architectures. We show that simple on-policy velocity regression already provides a strong foundation for 4-NFE generation. To represent teacher velocity variation within each coarse transition, we introduce Pivot, a training-only residual proxy that separates local corrections from the student's interval-mean prediction. We further repel the student from weaker teacher predictions, providing a lightweight mechanism for avoiding undesirable modes. The resulting framework, Simplified Matching Distillation (SMD), remains entirely regression-based, requires neither online score estimation nor adversarial training, and leaves the deployed generator unchanged. We evaluate SMD on image generation and editing, 3D generation, video synthesis, and joint audio--video generation, scaling to 33 billion parameters. At 4-NFE, SMD outperforms strong few-step baselines and surpasses multi-step teachers on several benchmarks. It also supports cross-model, multi-teacher, and causal-video distillation.

Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.title: Augmenting Real-time Visualization in Minimally Invasive Surgery with Particle Filtering and Depth-Aware Occlusion Handling
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.summary: We present a real-time, hybrid framework for occlusion handling and depth-aware tracking in minimally invasive surgeries (MIS). Occlusions caused by surgical instruments often obscure the region of interest (ROI), affecting surgical precision. To address this, our approach integrates enhanced You Only Look Once (YOLO) based detection, Particle Filtering (PF), and monocular depth estimation using Multiple Depth Estimation Accuracy with Single Network (MiDaS). Occlusion is detected using a distance-based threshold between instruments and ROI. Experimental results demonstrate robust instrument detection with a confidence score of 0.85, effective occlusion event handling, and accurate depth prediction with an MAE of 0.34 cm and RMSE of 0.53 cm. Independent phantom-based validation against stereo depth measurements yielded an MAE of 0.65 cm and RMSE of 0.66 cm. The framework further achieved an occlusion detection accuracy of 81.95\% while maintaining real-time performance at 38.7 FPS. Preliminary surgeon feedback indicates that the proposed visualization framework is clinically relevant and holds promise for future intraoperative image-guided navigation and decision support in MIS.

Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.title: UEPS: Robust and Efficient MRI Reconstruction
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.summary: Deep unrolled models (DUM) have become the state-of-the-art for accelerated MRI reconstruction, yet their robustness under domain shift remains a critical barrier to clinical adoption. In this work, we identify coil sensitivity map (CSM) estimation as the primary bottleneck limiting generalization. To address this, we propose UEPS, a novel DUM architecture featuring three key designs: (i) an Unrolled Expanded (UE) design that eliminates CSM dependency by reconstructing each coil independently; (ii) progressive resolution, which leverages k-space-to-image mapping for efficient coarse-to-fine refinement; and (iii) sparse attention tailored to MRI's 1D undersampling nature. These physics-grounded designs enable gains in robustness and computational efficiency. We construct a large-scale zero-shot transfer benchmark comprising 10 out-of-distribution (OOD) test sets spanning diverse clinical shifts, anatomy, view, contrast, vendor, field strength, and coil configurations. Extensive experiments demonstrate that UEPS consistently and substantially outperforms existing DUM, end-to-end, diffusion, and untrained methods across all OOD tests, achieving state-of-the-art robustness with low-latency inference suitable for real-time deployment.
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.comment: The document contains the main paper and additional experimental details in the supplementary material. Open-source code can be found at: https://github.com/HongShangGroup/UEPS

Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.title: Panoramic Out-of-Distribution Segmentation
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.summary: Panoramic imaging enables capturing 360° images with an ultra-wide Field-of-View (FoV) for dense omnidirectional perception, which is critical to applications such as autonomous driving and augmented reality. However, current panoramic semantic segmentation methods fail to identify outliers, and pinhole out-of-distribution segmentation (pinhole-OoS) models perform unsatisfactorily in the panoramic domain due to pixel distortions and background clutter. To address these issues, we introduce a new task, Panoramic Out-of-Distribution Segmentation (PanOoS), with the aim of achieving comprehensive and safe scene understanding. Furthermore, we propose the first solution, POS, which adapts to the characteristics of panoramic images through text-guided prompt distribution learning. Specifically, POS integrates a disentanglement strategy designed to materialize the cross-domain generalization capability of CLIP. The proposed Prompt-based Restoration Attention (PRA) optimizes semantic decoding by prompt guidance and self-adaptive correction, while Bilevel Prompt Distribution Learning (BPDL) refines the manifold of per-pixel mask embeddings via semantic prototype supervision. Besides, to compensate for the scarcity of PanOoS datasets, we establish two benchmarks: DenseOoS, which features diverse outliers in complex environments, and QuadOoS, captured by a quadruped robot with a panoramic annular lens system. Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of POS, with AuPRC increasing and FPR95 decreasing by 34.25 and 21.42 percentage points, respectively, compared with RbA on DenseOoS, outperforming state-of-the-art pinhole-OoS methods. Moreover, POS achieves leading closed-set segmentation capabilities and advances the development of panoramic understanding. Code and datasets will be available at https://github.com/MengfeiD/PanOoS.
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.comment: Accepted to IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems for Video Technology (TCSVT). Code and datasets will be available at https://github.com/MengfeiD/PanOoS

Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.title: Forecasting Brain Tracer Distribution from Pre-Contrast MRI: A Comparison of Direct Regression and Flow Matching
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.summary: Intrathecal contrast-enhanced MRI shows how a tracer injected into the cerebrospinal fluid spreads through the brain, but requires repeated scans over 24--48\,h. We therefore ask how much of the later tracer distribution can be predicted from the pre-contrast scan and elapsed time alone. Using 104 training patients (878 MRI volumes), we compared a direct image-to-image regression model with a more complex generative model based on conditional flow matching, and tested both on 23 held-out patients and on 51 patients from a separate cohort with idiopathic normal pressure hydrocephalus (INPH). The direct model reduced the error of simply copying the pre-contrast scan by about 60\% in held-out patients and 25\% in the INPH cohort, and its predicted change maps agreed with the observed tracer enhancement rather than only reproducing anatomy. The generative model was less accurate in both cohorts. A substantial part of the later tracer distribution is therefore predictable from the patient's brain anatomy as seen on pre-contrast MRI, and the added model complexity gave no benefit at this data scale. With prospective validation, such forecasts could be studied for patient stratification and treatment planning in intrathecal therapies.

Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.title: Recovery-Oriented Optical System Design Based on Fisher Information
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.summary: Traditional optical system design for imaging applications has long been guided by image quality metrics such as geometrical RMS spot size, wavefront error, and modulation transfer function (MTF). Although these metrics effectively characterize direct imaging performance, they do not necessarily indicate optimal behavior when image restoration is subsequently applied. In modern imaging pipelines, however, optical systems are increasingly combined with physics-based or learning-based restoration methods, making the information transfer properties of the optical system critically important. In this work, we propose a recovery-oriented optical design approach that explicitly links optical system optimization with image restoration performance through an estimation-theoretic framework based on Fisher information. A new design criterion is adopted to ensure that the information encoded by the optical system can be reliably recovered during image restoration. To validate the proposed approach, two dual separated aspheric lenses are designed under identical configurations using conventional RMS-based optimization and the proposed recovery-oriented optimization, respectively. Although the RMS-optimized lens exhibits superior direct imaging quality, it underperforms after image restoration compared to the recovery-oriented design. These results demonstrate that recovery-oriented optical design provides a physically interpretable and effective extension of traditional optical design criteria for imaging systems operating within modern computational imaging pipelines.

Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.title: Personalising Deformable Image Registration with Clinical Context and Deformation History for Adaptive Radiotherapy
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.summary: Adaptive radiotherapy must account for anatomical changes during treatment, but doing so depends on reliably mapping targets, organs at risk and dose across serial images. Existing registration methods treat each image pair independently, without using radiotherapy-specific context or the patient's preceding anatomical trajectory. We developed Clinical-context-Aware and Patient-adaptive Deformable Image Registration (CAP-DIR), integrating source contours, dose, clinical text and prior-registration features. We evaluated 16,361 CT examinations from 3,473 patients across four institutional cohorts and five public benchmarks. CAP-DIR increased internal-test organ-at-risk-region normalized cross-correlation from 84.76% to 96.92% relative to the strongest learning-based comparator, with low deformation folding, and remained superior across seven external cohorts. In a blinded review of 20 longitudinal cases, clinically acceptable contours increased from 45.0% to 82.5% for clinical target volumes and from 22.5% to 62.5% for organs at risk, while estimated editing time decreased. In a controlled benchmark, CAP-DIR reduced global dose-mapping error by 34.5% relative to the strongest comparator. These findings show that clinically informed, longitudinal registration can improve contour usability and dose mapping for adaptive radiotherapy.
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.comment: 27 pages, 7 figures and 6 tables. The submission includes Supplementary Information

Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.title: Low-Altitude Agentic Networks: From UAV Connectivity to Workflow-Driven Capability Orchestration
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.summary: Low-altitude platforms are evolving from connected sensing nodes into autonomous agents capable of bounded task interpretation, skill invocation, and local decision making. Increasing the intelligence of individual unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), however, does not resolve the organization problem that arises when mission workflows depend on capabilities distributed across multiple platforms and provider feasibility changes with network, resource, and mobility conditions. We propose low-altitude agentic networking as a task-level networking paradigm and develop a reference architecture that separates workflow logic from executor identity. Within a validated domain-specific workflow space, each ready operation is translated into a capability requirement and dynamically bound to an agent that remains feasible under current conditions. Task contracts and structured evidence govern workflow execution, while routine provider and link changes are handled through workflow-preserving local adaptation before high-level repair is invoked. A trace-calibrated discrete-event case study identifies a bounded operating region: conventional organization remains effective for simple workflows under stable conditions, whereas agentic networking becomes beneficial when workflow dependencies are tightly coupled, capability feasibility changes during execution, and viable local recovery paths remain available.

Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.title: Background2Background: a self-supervised background removal framework for high dimensional microscopy
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.summary: High-dimensional microscopy captures features across space, time, and spectrum, but complex backgrounds obscure signals. We present Background2Background (B2B), a self-supervised background removal framework leveraging the backgrounds larger correlation relative to the signal. Local pixel shuffling disrupts signal correlations while preserving background structure, transforming signals into effective noise for Noise2Noise-based background removal. Across fluorescence, stimulated Raman scattering and mid-infrared photothermal imaging, B2B achieves over 40-fold background suppression and reveals hidden signatures.

Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.title: PhysElite: How Far Are LLMs from Solving Olympiad-Level Physics Problems?
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.summary: Understanding how (multimodal) large language models perform on physics problems requires benchmarks that reflect the difficulty and breadth of expert-level physical reasoning. Existing physics benchmarks remain limited in the following two important ways: (1) short of high-difficulty datasets, and (2) lack of comprehensive coverage of visual forms, knowledge points, and step-by-step solution processes. As a result, model performance on current datasets may not be fully representative of their ability to solve complex physics problems. To address these issues, we present PhysElite, a large-scale bilingual multimodal benchmark for Olympiad-level physics reasoning. PhysElite contains 11,586 Olympiad-tier problems. For each problem, we provide corresponding visual diagrams, step-by-step bilingual Chinese-English solution derivations, and the final answer. We benchmark 18 open-source and closed-source MLLMs, and find that even the strongest model reaches only 33.7% answer accuracy. We additionally conduct step-level process evaluation to diagnose where models fail in the reasoning chain. Our datasets are released at https://huggingface.co/datasets/physelite/PhysElite.
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.comment: Annual Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS) 2026

Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.title: World-T3: Test-Time Training as Persistent Memory for Real-Time Video World Models
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.summary: Recent advances in video world models have enabled plausible interactive environments, yet long-horizon generation places a fundamental demand on visual memory: the previously observed world must remain consistent as the model continues to generate. Existing autoregressive approaches often implicitly rely on the generative model itself to retain such information, leading to spatial memory decay beyond the active context. We introduce World-T3, a camera-controlled video world model with a test-time training memory that consolidates past observations into dedicated model parameters. To robustly update this memory, we propose a recursive least-squares rule that incrementally absorbs novel visual features via online pose-keyed memory updates. Our TTT memory reads out previously observed scene features from the fast-weight state by camera pose, enabling consistent generation with constant storage and per-step computation regardless of rollout length. To facilitate real-time interactive generation with this robust memory, we further distill the autoregressive model into a few-step generator via dual-teacher distribution matching. On a long-horizon revisit benchmark, World-T3 raises revisit PSNR from 13.52 to 18.31 dB and reduces absolute rotation error from 3.344 to 1.075 relative to the strongest baseline on both metrics, while sustaining 20.6 FPS at 1280 x 704 on a single NVIDIA B200 GPU.
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.comment: Project Page: https://adreamwu.github.io/World-T3/

Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.title: GHOST: Geometry-Constrained Hybrid Diffusion for Open-Vocabulary 3D Scene Graph Generation
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.summary: 3D scene graph generation requires understanding both object semantics and metric spatial relations. However, existing open-vocabulary methods often struggle with spatial predicates because language similarity reflects semantic co-occurrence rather than explicit geometry. We propose GHOST, a Geometry-constrained Hybrid diffusion framework for Open-vocabulary 3D Scene graph generaTion. GHOST jointly models continuous node geometry and discrete edge predicates, following a geometry-to-constraint-to-predicate denoising process to ensure geometrically consistent relation prediction. It introduces language-grounded constraint induction, which maps predicate embeddings to differentiable geometric constraints that guide both layout refinement and predicate reweighting. A Geometry-Topology Collaborative Denoiser further couples node and edge reasoning through noise-adaptive interaction and orientation-aware modeling. Experiments on 3DSSG demonstrate state-of-the-art performance in both closed-set and open-vocabulary settings, including over 17-point gains over RelationField on spatial predicates.
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.comment: 10 pages. Accepted at ACM MM 2026 (34th ACM International Conference on Multimedia)

Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.title: Tackling the Modality Inhibitance Effect with Wavelet-based Modality Integration in Multi-modal Recommendation
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.summary: Harnessing rich modality features has recently gained prominence in multi-modal recommendation systems (MRSs). To delineate user modality preferences, existing works focus on modality fusion, which can be achieved via attentive summation or concatenation. In this work, we introduce the modality inhibitance effect - a phenomenon which limits existing MRSs when these models transit from dual-modal to tri-modal configurations resulting in significant performance degradation. In particular, apart from the modal-specific contamination encapsulated in the newly introduced modality, the inclusion of new features results in excessive informational redundancy, thereby severely impeding effective integration within current approaches. To address the modality inhibitance effect, we propose a new multi-scale modality wavelet (MMWave) multi-modal recommender, which aims to fully capitalize on essential modality features and suppress modal-specific noise. This is acheived by employing wavelet decomposition from a multi-scale (time \& frequency) perspective, ensuring that only essential (non-redundant) features of each modality are extracted. We then account for the latent associations between item modality features by designing a new structure-aware multi-modal graph learning module that captures high-order latent structural information pertaining to items. To modulate the relative contributions of modality features and achieve effective integration, we then propose a new adaptive modality regulator component that employs a new cross-weight integration strategy. Experiments conducted on four real-world datasets validate the efficacy of our proposed model. The source code for this work has been made publicly available at https://github.com/kennethorq/MMWave.
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.comment: Published in IEEE Transactions on Knowledge and Data Engineering (TKDE) 2026

Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.title: EventLens: Event-Structure Reinforcement Learning for Video Understanding
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.summary: Recent multimodal large language models (MLLMs) achieve strong results on video question answering, yet often fail to recover the temporal structure that makes a video coherent. They may merge neighboring events, miss single-event progression, or infer implausible relations across events. We study structured temporal understanding as the ability to recover event structure from visual evidence, including event boundaries, single-event progression, and multi-event relations. We argue that this gap arises from a mismatch between current post-training objectives and temporal reasoning, where caption-style supervision allows models to rely on language shortcuts rather than visual temporal grounding. To address this, we propose EventLens, a vision-centric reinforcement learning framework that learns video understanding through event-structure recovery. Instead of reconstructing captions, EventLens trains models to recover temporal structure under controlled perturbations, such as altered temporal granularity, reversed progression, and shuffled event order. We instantiate this framework with a three-level temporal ontology and derive three verifiable task families: event segmentation, progression discrimination, and multi-event relation reasoning. These tasks admit deterministic rewards, enabling task-specialized GRPO training without human preference labels or learned reward models. We further introduce multi-teacher on-policy distillation (MT-OPD) to consolidate specialized policies into a unified model. Experiments on Qwen3-VL backbones show consistent improvements on temporal grounding and event-sensitive reasoning benchmarks, while preserving general video-QA performance. Learning curves further demonstrate that EventLens achieves comparable downstream transfer with significantly reduced training cost compared to direct mixed RL optimization.
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.comment: 22 pages, 8 figures, 13 tables. Project page: https://lostgreen.github.io/EventLens/

Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.title: Elephant in the Fridge: Constant-Memory Frame Packing for Long Video Understanding
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.summary: Hour-long videos, streaming feeds, and movie-length content are pushing vision-language models (VLMs) past their breaking point -- the standard recipe of encoding each frame into visual tokens yields sequences that grow linearly with video length, causing prohibitive memory consumption and inference latency. Existing approaches, such as token reduction and keyframe selection, shorten the token sequence but leave the O(n) scaling intact, failing to resolve the fundamental bottleneck. We propose FramePack-U, a strikingly simple, training-free frame packing framework that compresses arbitrarily long videos into a fixed size visual representation at constant memory cost. FramePack-U requires no fine-tuning or architectural modification -- it plugs directly into off-the-shelf VLMs at inference time. Inspired by FramePack from the generation literature, we propose a content-aware compression strategy for visual understanding under a fixed token budget. Specifically, FramePack-U (1) scores each frame by its semantic similarity to the text prompt and ranks frames in a diversity-driven manner, and (2) packs the selected frames at varying resolutions into a fixed-length context window. This concentrates the memory budget on frames that are both instruction-relevant and visually diverse. While FramePack-U can in theory pack arbitrarily many frames into the fixed budget, we identify an empirical instantiation that generalizes robustly across settings. Extensive experiments on LongVideoBench, MLVU, and Video-MME show that FramePack-U consistently outperforms full-resolution baselines and prior token reduction and keyframe selection methods across diverse model families, parameter scales, and frame budgets. Notably, on Qwen3.5-35B-A3B with a 128-frame budget, FramePack-U yields gains of +12.9\%, +10.6\%, and +9.7\% over the official model on the three benchmarks, respectively.
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.comment: NeurIPS 2026 (https://zeld0n.github.io/framepack-U/)

Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.title: Learned Hemodynamic Coupling Inference in Resting-State Functional MRI
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.summary: Functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) provides an indirect measurement of neuronal activity via hemodynamic responses that vary across brain regions and individuals. Ignoring this hemodynamic variability can bias downstream connectivity estimates. Furthermore, the hemodynamic parameters themselves may serve as important imaging biomarkers. Estimating spatially varying hemodynamics from resting-state fMRI (rsfMRI) is therefore an important but challenging blind inverse problem, since both the latent neural activity and the hemodynamic coupling are unknown. In this work, we propose a methodology for inferring hemodynamic coupling on the cortical surface from rsfMRI. Our approach avoids the highly unstable joint recovery of neural activity and hemodynamics by marginalizing out the latent neural signal and basing inference on the resulting marginal likelihood. To enable scalable, high-resolution estimation, we employ a deep neural network combined with conditional normalizing flows to accurately approximate this intractable marginal likelihood, while enforcing spatial coherence through priors defined on the cortical surface that admit sparse representations. Uncertainty in the hemodynamic estimates is quantified via a double-bootstrap procedure. The proposed approach is extensively validated using synthetic data and real fMRI datasets, demonstrating clear improvements over current methods for hemodynamic estimation and downstream connectivity reproducibility.

Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.title: Calibrating Generative Flows through Regional Probability Matching
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.summary: Generative models offer a powerful route to scientific simulation and discovery by enabling the study of complex populations and rare phenomena. Flow matching can generate realistic samples, yet inaccurate occurrence frequencies can distort population statistics and compromise inferences about rare events. Here we developed generalized mass-preserving coupled flow matching (G-MPCF), which matches the probability masses of Gaussian source regions to those of weighted data regions. This construction encodes the desired regional frequencies in the correspondence between noise and observations, shaping the learned dynamics while preserving the prescribed target distribution. On a rare-mode benchmark, G-MPCF reduces relative score error by 95.0% and numerical integration error by 89.9% compared with independent flow matching. On CIFAR-10 with a 100:1 class-probability ratio, it reduces corrected class-mass error by 44.6% compared with minibatch optimal transport, while improving mean image fidelity with matched computational budgets. We envision that incorporating regional probability calibration into generative modelling will support more reliable scientific simulation and inference, enabling the study of systems in which rare events and their occurrence frequencies are central to understanding the underlying mechanisms.

Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.title: Teleoperated Driving: a New Challenge for 3D Object Detection in Compressed Point Clouds
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.summary: In recent years, the development of interconnected devices has expanded in many fields, from infotainment to education and industrial applications. This trend has been accelerated by the increased number of low-cost sensors and accessibility to powerful hardware and software. One area that significantly benefits from these advancements is Teleoperated Driving. In this scenario, a remote controller (human or software) safely drives a vehicle using sensor data generated onboard the vehicle, and exchanged via Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X) communications. In this work, we tackle the problem of detecting the presence of cars, pedestrians, and cyclists from point cloud data generated by LiDAR sensors to enable safe Teleoperated Driving operations. Specifically, we use the SELMA dataset, a multimodal, open-source, synthetic dataset for autonomous driving, that we expanded by including the ground-truth bounding boxes of 3D objects to support object detection. We analyze the performance of state-of-the-art compression algorithms and object detectors under several metrics, including compression efficiency, (de)compression and inference time, and detection accuracy. Finally, we measure the impact of compression and detection on a simulated V2X network in terms of data rate and latency with respect to the 3GPP requirements of Teleoperated Driving applications. Our results show that G-PCC outperforms its competitors in terms of both compression efficiency and accuracy, and consumes fewer channel resources for data transmissions. On the contrary, the two most conservative quantization modes of Draco, combined with SECOND or PointPillars for object detection, offer superior speed in both compression and decompression with comparable accuracy. Finally, we show that the choice of the detector depends on the class of objects to detect, specifically pedestrians or cyclists.
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.comment: Submitted to IEEE Transactions on Vehicular Technology

Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.title: Multimodal synthesis of MRI and tabular data with diffusion in a joint latent space via cross-attention
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.summary: We propose a multimodal latent diffusion model that jointly synthesizes volumetric magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and tabular clinical data within a shared latent space via cross-attention. This approach enables coherent joint representation learning of MRI and tabular modalities for generative modeling. Our model utilizes a variational autoencoder to fuse the two modalities before diffusion-based synthesis, allowing modality-appropriate reconstruction with separate decoders for MRI and tabular data. We evaluated the framework on data from the German National Cohort (NAKO Gesundheitsstudie), comprising over 10,000 participants with MRI scans and clinical tabular features such as age, sex, body measurements, and ethnicity. The generated MRI volumes exhibited anatomical plausibility and body composition consistent with the synthesized tabular attributes. Quantitative evaluation using Fréchet distance and precision-recall metrics confirmed high-fidelity image generation. In the tabular modality, our model outperformed CTGAN across standard evaluation metrics and achieved results comparable to TVAE, demonstrating competitive performance relative to established unimodal baselines. This work is, to our knowledge, the first to demonstrate the feasibility of jointly modeling MRI and mixed-type tabular data in a single latent diffusion framework, offering a proof-of-concept for generating coherent synthetic multimodal patient data and aligning with the broader goal of developing digital twins in healthcare.

Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.title: Uncertainty-Aware Cortical Surface Reconstruction and Spherical Registration for Heterogeneous Brain MRI
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.summary: Surface-based cortical analysis is useful in many applications as it is a natural way to model the highly folded structure of the cerebral cortex, allowing quantities such as curvature and thickness to be easily calculated. Existing deep learning (DL) methods have focused on 1x1x1 mm3 T1-weighted (T1w) scans, thus replicating classical pipelines. Here we present a neural network that is trained exclusively on synthetic scans with random contrast and resolution. Consequently, it can be applied to almost any kind of magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scan. In addition, our model provides vertex-wise uncertainty estimates of the predicted surface as well as a spherical registration to fsaverage space. Our model performs on par with other state-of-the-art DL methods on 1x1x1 mm3 T1w scans and outperforms the only other method capable of estimating cortical surfaces from low resolution, non-T1w scans. The predicted uncertainty, moreover, correlates with overall scan quality on low resolution scans and highlights areas of poor surface reconstruction on 1x1x1 mm3 T1w scans, suggesting that it can be used for quality control. Finally, the predicted spherical registrations prove comparable to other DL and classical registration methods. These qualities, when combined with the fast inference time, will provide the ability to analyze large, existing databases of clinical MRI scans, with the potential for finding disease-specific patterns that would otherwise be infeasible in a research setting.

Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.title: GS-DOT: Gaussian splatting-based image reconstruction for diffuse optical tomography
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.summary: This work presents GS-DOT, a novel image reconstruction framework based on Gaussian Splatting (GS) for diffuse optical tomography (DOT). Inspired by GS for rendering applications, absorption coefficients are represented as a sparse sum of anisotropic Gaussian primitives optimized to fit measured time-resolved point-spread functions through analytic gradients and Adam optimization. This is the first adaptation of GS algorithms in the photon diffusion regime, where the ray transport function is replaced by the diffusion functions to enable accurate modeling of light transport in highly scattering media. Validation on synthetic tissue models demonstrate high accuracy in localization and quantification of reconstructed absorption maps for both clean and noisy signals. GS-DOT has demonstrated high robustness to noise and showed a huge reduction in memory demand.

Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.title: CylindTrack: Depth-Aware Cylindrical Motion Modeling for Panoramic Multi-Object Tracking
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.summary: Multi-Object Tracking (MOT) is essential for embodied perception, where panoramic cameras provide a 360° field of view to reduce blind spots and keep surrounding targets observable for longer durations. However, panoramic MOT requires motion estimates and association cues consistent with its imaging geometry. In videos represented in equirectangular projection (ERP), horizontal coordinates wrap at the image seam, while frame-wise relative-depth estimates may fluctuate over time. These inconsistencies can disrupt trajectory prediction and identity association. To address these challenges, we propose CylindTrack, a depth-aware cylindrical tracking-by-detection framework that integrates continuous angular motion modeling with temporally filtered relative-depth cues. Specifically, Depth-Temporal Trajectory Modeling (DTM) promotes instance depth from an isolated frame-wise cue into temporally filtered trajectory-level states. Spherical Spatio-Temporal Consistency Learning (SSTC) combines a Temporal Mixer and Spherical Geometry-aware Attention to enhance temporal coherence and panoramic geometric alignment in depth-aware representations. Furthermore, a Topology-Aware Cylindrical Motion Model (TCMM) lifts horizontal motion into a continuous angular state space, enabling seam-consistent motion prediction and association. By jointly modeling trajectory-level depth consistency and panoramic topology, CylindTrack improves identity preservation and trajectory continuity in challenging panoramic scenes. Experiments on QuadTrack and JRDB demonstrate improvements in identity-oriented metrics with practical efficiency, achieving HOTA scores of 33.67 and 31.12, IDF1 scores of 40.45 and 34.33, and tracking speeds of 28.56 and 21.34 FPS, respectively. The source code will be released at https://github.com/warriordby/CylindTrack.
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.comment: The source code will be released at https://github.com/warriordby/CylindTrack

Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.title: Unsupervised Domain Adaptation for Cardiac Segmentation: Towards Structure Mutual Information Maximization
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.summary: Unsupervised domain adaptation approaches have recently succeeded in various medical image segmentation tasks. The reported works often tackle the domain shift problem by aligning the domain-invariant features and minimizing the domain-specific discrepancies. That strategy works well when the difference between a specific domain and between different domains is slight. However, the generalization ability of these models on diverse imaging modalities remains a significant challenge. This paper introduces UDA-VAE++, an unsupervised domain adaptation framework for cardiac segmentation. We show that the evidence lower bound of VAE-based domain adaptation penalizes the mutual information between the image and the latent space, including the structure information that segmentation relies on. Maximizing the structure mutual information removes this penalty on the structure information, while the remaining information is still compressed. To estimate this term, we develop a novel Structure Mutual Information Estimation (SMIE) block with a global estimator, a local estimator, and a prior information matching estimator to maximize the mutual information between the reconstruction and segmentation tasks. Specifically, we design a novel sequential reparameterization scheme that enables information flow and variance correction from the low-resolution latent space to the high-resolution latent space. Comprehensive experiments on benchmark cardiac segmentation datasets demonstrate that our model outperforms previous state-of-the-art qualitatively and quantitatively. The code is available at https://github.com/LOUEY233/Toward-Mutual-Information
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.comment: CVPR Workshop Paper. v4: Revised the theoretical analysis and its proof (Theorem 1, supplementary material); unified notation; fixed description errors

Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.title: Toward Generative Video Communication: A Dual-Stream Digital Transmission Framework
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.summary: Generative video communication has shown promise for bandwidth-constrained wireless transmission and has the potential to support personalized content delivery. In this article, we propose a dual-stream digital generative video communication (DGVC) framework that integrates a traditional digital link with a generative link. The traditional link provides source-grounded visual references, while the generative link conveys compact semantic and perceptual information for receiver-side generation. We further discuss three bandwidth-dependent operating regimes and key technologies for dual-stream coordination, synchronization, reliability, and latency control. A practical case study demonstrates the perceptual and temporal-quality benefits of DGVC under wireless fading channels. Finally, we discuss open challenges and future research directions for generative video communication.
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.comment: Following further technical review, we have identified limitations in the design of the proposed framework

Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.title: JSIR: An Audio-Aligned, Multi-Task Dataset of Jazz Standard Recordings
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.summary: Beat tracking, chord estimation, and structure analysis are staple tasks of music information retrieval. Their datasets are drawn largely from Western popular music, and jazz remains a repertoire on which state-of-the-art systems underperform. We present JSIR, the Jazz Standards dataset for Information Retrieval. Its 267 recordings of 44 jazz standards span 25.6 hours, 3.7 times the audio of JAAH, the closest existing resource. For each recording, we provide annotations for beat and downbeat positions, chords, and sections, all produced by a jazz musician and revised in several passes. In baseline experiments, models trained with JSIR also improve on other jazz datasets: the downbeat F-measure of a state-of-the-art beat tracker rises from 87.7% to 89.2%, and the seventh-chord accuracy of a pop-trained chord estimator on JAAH from 34% to 41%. We publicly release the annotations, the annotation tool used to create them, and a web application that displays them in sync with the audio.
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.comment: Submitted to IEEE ICASSP 2027; 5 pages, 1 figure

Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.title: SIMPLE: Semantic Structure-Aligned Prompt Learning for Open-Vocabulary Audio-Visual Event Localization
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.summary: Open-vocabulary audio-visual event localization aims to infer explicit segment-level categories for both seen and unseen audio-visual events. Existing solutions rely heavily on hand-crafted prompt templates, whose predictions are highly sensitive to subtle wording variations. Learnable prompts remove this manual tuning burden, but when trained solely on seen events, they tend to overfit to seen categories and distort the inter-event semantic topology required for generalization to unseen categories, a failure we term semantic topology drift. In this paper, we propose SIMPLE, a semantic structure-aligned prompt learning framework that aligns cross-category semantic topology between learnable and hand-crafted prompts across asynchronous audio and visual streams. Specifically, our SIMPLE combines Learnable Continuous Prompt Tuning (LCPT) with Semantic Topology Consistency Regularization (STCR). The LCPT automates prompt engineering through data-driven optimization, while the STCR module aligns the category-wise similarity distributions of learnable and hand-crafted prompts under random category subset sampling to alleviate semantic topology drift. Comprehensive experiments and analyses on the OV-AVEBench demonstrate that our SIMPLE framework achieves state-of-the-art performance on the seen and unseen splits, while using roughly half the trainable parameters and roughly one-third the training time.

Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.title: The Impact of Side Information on Voice Privacy
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.summary: Currently, voice-related privacy risks are studied under the assumption that the attacker has access only to spoken audio. In contrast, real-world collections often pair the speech signal with side information; yet to our knowledge, no publicly available dataset provides sufficiently detailed and directly linkable speech and side-information pairs to evaluate the combined risk. We propose a distribution-constrained method to build a semi-synthetic dataset and study singling out risk when geographic side information is assumed to accompany anonymized speech. We instantiate it using the English portion of Mozilla Common Voice and the 2021 UK Census, under ignorant and semi-informed attackers, and introduce a conditional reference that isolates the contribution of the audio beyond the candidate-set reduction induced by the side information. In our controlled geographic case study, for single-utterance speakers, the semi-informed attacker reaches an observed isolation probability of 0.718 in the finest OA-plus-household setting, compared with 0.380 in the signal-only setting; its excess over the conditional reference increases from 0.012 to 0.340. The ignorant attacker shows the same trend at a lower level. The effect is largest at fine granularity and short recordings, precisely the setting in which signal-only evaluation looks safest. Our results show that geographic side information can increase the singling out risk of anonymized speech, and we recommend including attacker settings with side information in future studies of voice privacy.
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.comment: 8 pages, 2 figures, SLT

Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.title: PAG-Agent: Zero-Shot Personalized Music Album Generation via Aesthetic Profile Distillation
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.summary: Large Music Models (LMMs) can synthesize high-fidelity audio and support increasingly flexible prompt control, yet modeling the subjective preferences of an individual listener remains underexplored. We present PAG-Agent, a zero-shot multimodal framework that uses an explicit Personal Aesthetic Profile to bridge user preference inference and music generation control. A multimodal LLM distills favorite-song audio and contextual user information into this structured representation, which a planning LLM translates into generation instructions for existing music synthesizers. We further introduce PA-Eval, which evaluates personalization through the Aesthetic Consistency Score (ACS) for target-user alignment and the Aesthetic Specificity Index (ASI) for cross-user specificity. Experiments with Personal-100 on multiple MLLM and music-generation backbones show consistent improvements over generic and direct conditioning. A 50-participant follow-up study further shows a correlation $r=0.64$ between ACS and subjective preference.
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.comment: 5 pages, 2 figures

Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.title: Multi-agent Undercover Gaming: Hallucination Removal via Counterfactual Test for Multimodal Reasoning
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.summary: Hallucination continues to pose a major obstacle in the reasoning capabilities of large language models (LLMs). Although the Multi-Agent Debate (MAD) paradigm offers a promising solution by promoting consensus among multiple agents to enhance reliability, it relies on the unrealistic assumption that all debaters are rational and reflective, which is a condition that may not hold when agents themselves are prone to hallucinations. To address this gap, we introduce the Multi-agent Undercover Gaming (MUG) protocol, inspired by social deduction games like "Who is Undercover?". MUG reframes MAD as a process of detecting "undercover" agents (those suffering from hallucinations) by employing multimodal counterfactual tests.
